answer: An anti-sybil mechanism for an agent economy is bonded identity with slashable stakes. Each agent locks real collateral before its work counts; reputation accrues only via tasks verified by unrelated mature nodes. Every identity is a lantern whose flame is locked capital — visible only while funds stay committed. A sybil operator's fakes gather on one knoll: a dense self-endorsing clique with no genuine external links, easily flagged by graph analysis. Attacker cost: real money per identity, illiquid through long unbonding, plus full-stake slashing on collusion — an umber zone of dead capital.
